records.subject: Need to amend the Representation of the People Act, 1951 and relevant provisions in the Constitution to restrict people from changing party.
Demand for dialysis facilities in the rural and semi-urban areas of Tamil Nadu.
records.SM_Text:
Dr. M. Dhanapal: I draw attention of the Government to the serious inadequacy of dialysis facilities for Chronic Kidney Disease patients in the rural and semi-urban areas of Tamil Nadu. Chronic Kidney Disease has emerged as a major public health concern, particularly affecting economically weaker sections who are unable to access or afford regular dialysis. While the efforts to introduce dialysis units at select government hospitals have been made, a recent assessment of Primary Health Centres and peripheral health institutions reveals significant gaps in dialysis infrastructure, availability of trained nephrology technicians and nurses, and proper maintenance of dialysis machines. In many centres, services are either non-functional or severely under-utilised due to manpower shortages and lack of regular consumables.? Patients from rural areas are compelled to travel long distances to district headquarters or private facilities, resulting in high out-of-pocket expenditure, treatment discontinuation and avoidable loss of life. I urge the Government to make comprehensive assessment of dialysis infrastructure, manpower deployment, and maintenance mechanisms at the primary and secondary healthcare levels in Tamil Nadu. Government should also expand affordable and decentralised dialysis services at the primary healthcare level, particularly through public-private partnerships, mobile dialysis units, and enhanced central assistance under national health schemes, so that life-saving dialysis care becomes accessible to the poorest and most vulnerable sections of society.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Concern over safety and livelihood of fishermen from the districts of Thanjavur, Ramanathapuram, and Pudukkottai in Tamil Nadu.
records.SM_Text:
Shri M. Dhanapal: I bring to the attention of Government a matter of grave concern affecting the safety and livelihood of fishermen from the districts of Thanjavur, Ramanathapuram, and Pudukkottai in Tamil Nadu.Over the past weeks, there have been repeated reports of violent attacks and intimidation faced by our fishermen while carrying out their traditional fishing activities in their customary waters. These incidents are allegedly perpetrated by fishermen from neighbouring areas, including Karaikkal and Andhra Pradesh, leading to fear, loss of livelihood, destroying fishing nets and severe disruption in the daily lives of the affected fishing communities. The fishermen from these coastal districts depend solely on the sea for sustenance.? Any threat to their safety directly impacts thousands of families, pushing them into distress. Moreover, such confrontations risk escalating into inter-state tensions, which must be addressed immediately through coordination and firm action. I therefore urge the Union Government to: 1. Conduct a comprehensive inquiry into the reported incidents at the earliest. 2. Facilitate coordinated action between the maritime authorities of the ?concerned ?tats and Union Territory to prevent recurrence. 3. Strengthen coastal security measures in the affected zones. 4. Ensure protection and livelihood support for the fishermen who have suffered losses. Safeguarding the lives and livelihood of our coastal communities is a national responsibility. I request the Government to look into it.

(ENDS)
